flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child was having a really hard moment emotionally. What did you notice about what they were feeling, and how did you respond?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q3 Attempt 1]
Some of the kids that I work with were autistic, and they have a lot of behavioral issues, and they were, you know, they were a little physical. So to calm them down, like I always sit down with them, give them hugs, breathe in with them, try to give them their favorite things that they like to calm them down and soothe them down. And so they were able to go back with the rest of the children. We kind of separate.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you felt overwhelmed at work with children present. What did you do to manage yourself?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q4 Attempt 1]
Hmm. I think I just try to breathe in as much as I can and drink water and just think positive. We all have hard days, so it's okay. Yes, I do. It was because, um, the child, okay. It was because the child was upset over his eating time. He didn't want to eat lunch and, um, I have, he had a specific rules and things that their parents wanted him to do or eat a specific times and he didn't want to eat. So he was really upset and he just throw all the food and start throwing the food in my face and stuff like that. Yeah.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Imagine you’re caring for a child who clearly does not want to be touched during a routine task, like diapering, helping with clothing, or guiding them physically. They are pulling away or saying no. Walk me through exactly what you would do, step by step
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q5 Attempt 1]
i would try to comfort him first i'll try to tell him it's okay that if he don't if he don't want me to do that if he is able to maybe help in a little bit so he's able to take off his own clothes and do it himself if that makes him feel more comfortable and then i would try to leave me as much as possible to touch just a lot when he's taking it out just kind of take pulling it away from himself fleeing and stuff like that when he needs a diaper change i will try to play with him tickle him or make her happy and disrupt him with other things so i could change him

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you received feedback you didn’t expect or didn’t fully agree with. What happened next?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q6 Attempt 1]
did i not fall angry with maybe when the child had a hard time and because of um the hard time that he was having just keeping him away for the rest of the classroom for a while instead of having them all go out at the same time i understand it's you know they need time to calm down and i know it if they don't calm down it could hurt others depending of what they have or what's going on at the time with in the families um but i didn't like it that he had to stay out of the activity for a while i would have wished they were all together integrated yeah

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time something didn’t go as planned at work and your role in it. How did you handle the responsibility piece?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q7 Attempt 1]
We do Cheerios to do activities sometimes for them to glue it into paper or do art and stuff like that so we could decorate the classroom. They were having a hard time with the Cheerios instead of putting it on the paper or because they couldn't do the necklace. So we decided to do it as an art. They were eating it. So they were just eating everything and it was just a mess. Yeah.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time you had to work closely with another adult in a challenging situation. How did you navigate it?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q8 Attempt 1]
i tried to tell them my point of view but if whatever with the classroom or whatever was going on but if they didn't like it they didn't feel comfortable with it i kind of just followed the lead to keep everything you know in harmony and just went with the flow of stuff and just supported the role the assistant or the teacher whatever they feel like it was best to do

flow_transcript_slices.question: Can you share something you’ve learned about children or yourself over time that changed how you approach your work?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q9 Attempt 1]
That they are all different and they all have different needs and that they all need to have a sense of belonging in the classroom so they could all feel integrated in the classroom. Because what works for that child is not going to work for the other child. So trying to be more open-minded, trying to find more ideas of things that I could do to accomplish those goals with that child and their needs. Thank you.

flow_transcript_slices.question: Tell me about a time a child’s behavior was challenging for you. How did you approach it?
flow_transcript_slices.candidate_transcript:
[Q10 Attempt 1]
A lot of patience. You have to be understandable. When I first started working, there were a couple of kids that have disabilities and they were integrated, you know, in the whole classroom of 12. And sometimes it was just by myself when, you know, the assistant had to go to another classroom. It was hard when one of the kids would go off and then the rest would go off. So just a lot of patience and I try to make it fun, try reading books, try doing puppets, laughing, or putting music, try to calm everybody.
